cells.tense: Right now you are carrying an impulse that has not yet been pointed anywhere.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Stay with whatever you already picked for another week — no fresh sign required, no better option weighed. Watch what holds.
cells.core:
Something in you has caught without being aimed. That's not confusion — it's the thing before the direction, and you can stand in it without forcing the shape. The path usually shows one step at a time; you're willing to let that be enough. When what you're carrying is allowed to stay unaimed around you, it takes a point of its own instead of borrowing one.

Keep going with the version you already chose — not the newer, sharper option. Go another week without demanding proof that it's right. The week is the test, not the answer, and nothing about your question gets settled by looking for a sign. If it holds, you'll notice it held, and you'll have learned that your own choosing carries further than you can see from here.

cells.tense: By the time the future arrives you will have needed it to be readable in advance.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Put one unclear situation out whole — every part at once — and look until deciding stops being a way of seeing more. Then leave it.
cells.core:
You're reaching for the whole road at once. There's a version of this where every step has to be visible before you take the first one, and you're bracing against a future that can't be written in from here. The light is enough for the next step; you're asking it for all of them. Wanting the full view is not a flaw — it's the same fire insisting on a target. But you've stopped letting the path reveal itself.

Lay one unclear situation out whole, every piece visible at once, and look until deciding stops being a way of seeing more. Then leave it alone. The look is the whole act, not preparation for a move. You'll know you saw it all not because the future got easier but because you no longer need it readable before you begin.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a threshold you already crossed a while back.
cells.act: name every feeling in it on one page, none of them crossed out
cells.ask: Pick something you're unsure about, write every feeling it brings onto a single page, and cross none of them out.
cells.core:
The beginning already happened and you're not quite through it. The uncertainty stopped being open and started being old — you're standing at a door that's behind you, waiting to feel arrived. The next step is there; you've been declining to take it while checking whether you're allowed. That's not a failure of nerve. It's a fire that ran out of match.

Let feeling lead, not thought. Name every feeling a situation brings you on one page — all of them, none crossed out, none ranked. Don't resolve them; just let them be complete. You know how to feel the whole of a thing, and doing it for yourself feeds the starved part from the side, not by pushing. When you move, the road still shows one step; you'll just be standing on it.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where you are already writing.
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Walk through something you made and finished, touch nothing, fix nothing — let it stand as it is.
cells.core:
You're doing the work — picking the direction, taking the step, following the thing where it goes — and calling it not really deciding, just seeing how it lands. The choices are good and they're being made. What's missing is any record that you made them. Circumstance gets the credit; what you started doesn't.

Walk through something you made and finished. Small is fine; done is the point. Touch nothing, fix nothing, don't reach past it toward the next version. Let the satisfaction of a finished thing land the way it does when someone else shows you their work. That's how a built thing tells you it was yours. Nothing has to be decided — only stop pretending the deciding wasn't you.

attempts.check: The draft most at risk is Balanced: I read the person as already carrying a direction that isn't pointed yet, and the record only supports that a spark is present and unshaped, not that they hold a star to follow. A reader could reasonably say the direction isn't hidden, it simply isn't there yet. The ask survives being wrong — going one more week with the version they already chose is useful whether or not the version turns out to be right, and it teaches them their own persistence either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is the Balanced core's 'the direction will find the fire' unless the ask makes it concrete enough to test.
